Customer (Michael Murray): You charged me far more in fees than the gas actually cost. That can't be right.

Agent (Kagiso Radebe): Is the property occupied at the moment?

Agent (Kagiso Radebe): The distribution charge and the fixed daily charge are set by the AUC for your rate class, so they apply even when the meter reads zero.
Agent (Kagiso Radebe): I've checked each line against your metered usage and the current rate schedule.
Customer (Michael Murray): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Kagiso Radebe): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Kagiso Radebe): I've gone through every line — the distribution charge and fixed monthly charge apply regardless of usage under your rate class, and I've corrected the one line item that was billed in error. You'll see the adjustment on your next statement.
Customer (Michael Murray): So one of them was actually wrong?
Agent (Kagiso Radebe): Yes, a late-payment charge was applied after your payment had already cleared. That's the adjustment.
Customer (Michael Murray): And the zero-usage charges?
Agent (Kagiso Radebe): Those are regulated and stay. The breakdown in your email explains each one.
Agent (Kagiso Radebe): To recap: the late-payment charge comes off on your next statement, and the line-by-line breakdown is in your email.
Customer (Michael Murray): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
